skills.title: Vector components and unit vectors
skills.task: Resolve a vector into components along given unit vectors, and find its magnitude and direction.

skills.title: Dot product and projections
skills.task: Compute $\vec a\cdot\vec b$ from components or from $|a||b|\cos\theta$, and use it to project a vector onto a direction.
prereqs: Components are what the dot product combines.

skills.title: Cross product and the right-hand rule
skills.task: Compute $\vec a\times\vec b$ from components, give its direction by the right-hand rule and its size $|a||b|\sin\theta$.

skills.title: A vector turning at a steady rate: dA/dt = Ω × A
skills.task: For a vector of fixed length turning about an axis at angular velocity $\vec\Omega$, write $d\vec A/dt=\vec\Omega\times\vec A$ and see that only the part of $\vec A$ perpendicular to $\vec\Omega$ changes.
prereqs: The rate of change is a cross product.
It is a time derivative of a vector.

skills.title: Derivatives and the chain rule
skills.task: Differentiate products and compositions, including time derivatives of functions of $\theta(t)$.

skills.title: Basic integrals
skills.task: Evaluate polynomial and simple trigonometric integrals, including by substitution.

skills.title: Integrals over a body: dm = λ dx, σ dA, ρ dV
skills.task: Set up an integral over a rod, a disk or a solid by choosing a mass element and its limits (slices, rings, shells).
prereqs: It ends in an ordinary integral.
Rings and shells use polar or spherical elements.

skills.title: Small-angle and first-order approximations
skills.task: Use $\sin\theta\approx\theta$, $\cos\theta\approx1-\theta^2/2$ and $(1+x)^n\approx1+nx$ to simplify an answer or an equation of motion.
prereqs: These are the first terms of Taylor series.

skills.title: The harmonic equation ẍ + ω²x = 0
skills.task: Recognize $\ddot x=-\omega^2x$ (after rewriting an equation of motion) and read off the angular frequency $\omega$; know the solution $A\cos(\omega t+\phi)$.
prereqs: The solution is checked by differentiating twice.

skills.title: Polar and cylindrical unit vectors r̂, φ̂, ẑ
skills.task: Use $\hat r$, $\hat\phi$ (and $\hat z$): express them in Cartesian components and know that $\hat r\times\hat\phi=\hat z$, $\hat z\times\hat r=\hat\phi$.
prereqs: Unit vectors are defined by their components.
The handedness relations are cross products.

skills.title: Matrix times vector; symmetric matrices
skills.task: Multiply a 3×3 matrix by a column vector, and recognize a symmetric matrix.
prereqs: The vector is handled through its components.

skills.title: Components in a rotated set of axes
skills.task: Write a vector's components along a tilted pair of perpendicular unit vectors, e.g. $\hat x=\cos\theta\,\hat e_3-\sin\theta\,\hat e_2$.
prereqs: A component is a dot product with a unit vector.

skills.title: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric matrix
skills.task: Find eigenvalues from $\det(A-\lambda I)=0$ and eigenvectors for a 2×2 or simple 3×3 symmetric matrix; know that its eigenvectors can be chosen orthogonal.
prereqs: The eigen-equation is a matrix acting on a vector.

skills.title: Checking units and dimensions
skills.task: Check that every term of an answer has the right units, and use dimensional analysis to reject a wrong formula.

skills.title: Checking limiting cases
skills.task: Test an answer by sending a parameter to 0 or ∞ (or θ to 0 or 90°) and comparing with the case you already understand.

skills.title: Newton's second and third laws
skills.task: Apply $\vec F_{net}=m\vec a$ to one particle, and pair action–reaction forces correctly.
prereqs: F = ma is applied component by component.

skills.title: Free-body diagrams
skills.task: Draw every force acting on each object (gravity, normal, friction, tension, pivot forces), and nothing else.
prereqs: A diagram is the input to F = ma.

skills.title: Circular motion: a = v²/r = rω² toward the center
skills.task: Give the centripetal acceleration of a point moving in a circle of radius $r$ at speed $v$ or angular speed $\omega$, and the net inward force it needs.
prereqs: The inward force comes from F = ma.

skills.title: Momentum and F_ext = dP/dt
skills.task: Use total momentum and $\vec F_{ext}=d\vec P/dt=M\vec a_{CM}$ for a system; conserve momentum when the external force vanishes.
prereqs: It follows from summing F = ma over particles.

skills.title: Center of mass and the CM frame
skills.task: Locate the center of mass, and split kinetic energy as $\tfrac12MV_{CM}^2$ plus the energy relative to the CM.

skills.title: Writing a Lagrangian and its E–L equations
skills.task: Write $L=T-V$ in convenient coordinates and apply $\frac{d}{dt}\frac{\partial L}{\partial\dot q}=\frac{\partial L}{\partial q}$.
prereqs: The equations are built from derivatives.
Compare with the F = ma result.

skills.title: Cyclic coordinates give conserved momenta
skills.task: Spot a coordinate that does not appear in $L$ and use the conserved $\partial L/\partial\dot q$.
prereqs: It is read off the E–L equation.

skills.title: Angular momentum of a particle: L = r × p
skills.task: Compute $\vec L=\vec r\times m\vec v$ about a chosen origin, and know it is conserved when the force on the particle is central about that origin.
prereqs: p = mv is the quantity being crossed.

skills.title: L_z = Iω for a flat body rotating about the z axis
skills.task: Write $L_z=I\omega$ with $I=\int r^2\,dm$ about the rotation axis for a pancake-shaped body.
prereqs: It is the sum of the particles' r × p.
I is an integral over the body.

skills.title: Rotational kinetic energy ½Iω²
skills.task: Use $KE=\tfrac12I\omega^2$ for rotation about a fixed axis.

skills.title: General plane motion: CM part plus rotation about the CM
skills.task: Split $L=\vec R_{CM}\times M\vec V_{CM}+I_{CM}\omega\,\hat z$ and $KE=\tfrac12MV_{CM}^2+\tfrac12I_{CM}\omega^2$.
prereqs: The spin part is I_CM ω.
The split is about the CM.

skills.title: Parallel-axis theorem
skills.task: Use $I=I_{CM}+Md^2$ for an axis a distance $d$ from a parallel axis through the CM.
prereqs: It relates two moments of inertia.

skills.title: Perpendicular-axis theorem (flat objects)
skills.task: Use $I_z=I_x+I_y$ for a flat object in the x-y plane, e.g. a disk about a diameter is $\tfrac14MR^2$.
prereqs: It relates moments of a flat body.

skills.title: L_z = I_z ω for 3D objects on a fixed axis
skills.task: For any rigid body rotating about the z axis, $L_z=I_z\omega$ with $I_z=\int(x^2+y^2)dm$; the other components of L need not vanish.

skills.title: Standard moments of inertia
skills.task: Recall I for a rod (center, end), ring, disk, solid sphere and spherical shell, and when to use which.
prereqs: These are values of the same integral.

skills.title: Computing I by integration
skills.task: Compute a moment of inertia by slicing a body into rods, rings, disks or shells and integrating.
prereqs: The definition of I is the integral.

skills.title: Moments of inertia of composite bodies
skills.task: Add the moments of the parts about one axis, moving each part with the parallel-axis theorem.
prereqs: Parts are shifted to the common axis.

skills.title: Torque τ = r × F about a chosen origin
skills.task: Compute a torque as $\vec r\times\vec F$ (or lever arm × force), with its direction, about a stated origin.

skills.title: τ = dL/dt about a fixed point or the CM
skills.task: Apply $\vec\tau=d\vec L/dt$ about a fixed origin or about the CM (even if it accelerates), and not about other accelerating points.
prereqs: The left side is a torque.
The right side is the change of L.
The CM version uses the CM split.

skills.title: Rolling without slipping: v = ωR
skills.task: Use $v_{CM}=\omega R$ and $a=\alpha R$, the contact point at rest, and static friction of either direction.
prereqs: Friction and normal forces must be drawn.
ω and I enter the dynamics.

skills.title: Rolling down an incline
skills.task: Derive $a=\dfrac{g\sin\theta}{1+I/MR^2}$ from F = ma plus τ = Iα (or from energy), and rank rolling objects.
prereqs: The constraint links a and α.

skills.title: Physical pendulum frequency
skills.task: Show $\omega=\sqrt{Mgd/I_{pivot}}$ for small oscillations about a pivot a distance d from the CM.
prereqs: Torque about the pivot drives it.
Read ω from the harmonic equation.

skills.title: Angular momentum conservation in collisions
skills.task: Conserve L about a pivot (or any point where the unknown impulsive forces act) through a collision, while linear momentum may not be conserved.
prereqs: No external torque about that point.

skills.title: Angular impulse from a blow
skills.task: For a blow $J$ at distance $d$ from the CM of a free body: $\Delta V_{CM}=J/M$ and $\Delta\omega=Jd/I_{CM}$.

skills.title: Center of percussion (sweet spot)
skills.task: Find where to strike a pivoted or held stick so the pivot feels no impulse (2L/3 for a uniform stick held at one end).
prereqs: It balances ΔV_CM against ω × distance.

skills.title: General motion: translation plus rotation
skills.task: Describe any rigid-body motion as the motion of one point plus a rotation about an axis through that point.
prereqs: The planar version of the same idea.

skills.title: The angular velocity vector; v = ω × r
skills.task: Give $\vec\omega$'s direction by the right-hand rule, and compute a point's velocity as $\vec v=\vec\omega\times\vec r$ (plus the reference point's velocity).

skills.title: Angular velocities add as vectors
skills.task: Add angular velocities, e.g. $\vec\omega=\vec\Omega+\omega'\hat e_3$ for a body spinning at ω′ relative to a frame that turns at Ω.
prereqs: They are vectors of this kind.

skills.title: The instantaneous axis passes through points at rest
skills.task: Find the direction of $\vec\omega$ from two points of the body that are momentarily at rest (e.g. a pivot and a contact point).
prereqs: Points on the axis have v = ω × r = 0.

skills.title: Rolling without slipping in 3D (cones, wheels on axles)
skills.task: Relate spin and precession rates of a rolling cone or wheel-and-axle using the contact point at rest, e.g. $\omega'=(R/r)\,\Omega$.
prereqs: The contact point is at rest.
ω = Ω + ω′ is split into precession and spin.

skills.title: L = I ω with the inertia tensor
skills.task: For rotation about an axis through the origin, compute $\vec L=\mathbf I\vec\omega$, and see that $\vec L$ need not be parallel to $\vec\omega$.
prereqs: The input is the vector ω.
L sums r × m v with v = ω × r.
I acts on ω as a matrix.

skills.title: Computing inertia-tensor components
skills.task: Compute $I_{xx}=\int(y^2+z^2)dm$ and $I_{xy}=-\int xy\,dm$ for point masses or simple bodies about a given origin.

skills.title: Kinetic energy: ½ ω·L
skills.task: Compute rotational kinetic energy as $\tfrac12\vec\omega\cdot\vec L=\tfrac12\vec\omega^T\mathbf I\vec\omega$.

skills.title: L of a moving body: CM part plus L about the CM
skills.task: For a body that translates and rotates, write $\vec L=\vec R\times M\vec V+\mathbf I_{CM}\vec\omega$.
prereqs: The spin part uses the tensor about the CM.

skills.title: Parallel-axis theorem for the inertia tensor
skills.task: Shift the tensor from the CM to another point: $I_{ij}=I^{CM}_{ij}+M(R^2\delta_{ij}-R_iR_j)$; for an axis this reduces to $+Md^2$.

skills.title: Principal axes: where L is parallel to ω
skills.task: State that a principal axis is one where $\mathbf I\vec\omega=\lambda\vec\omega$, that every body has three orthogonal ones about any point, and that I is diagonal in that basis.
prereqs: It is a property of L = Iω.

skills.title: Principal axes from symmetry
skills.task: Name the principal axes of a symmetric body about a point on its symmetry axis: the symmetry axis and every axis perpendicular to it (equal moments).

skills.title: Principal axes by solving the eigenvalue problem
skills.task: Find principal moments and axes of a given inertia tensor by solving $\det(\mathbf I-\lambda)=0$.

skills.title: Writing L along principal axes
skills.task: Split $\vec\omega$ along the principal axes, then $\vec L=I_1\omega_1\hat e_1+I_2\omega_2\hat e_2+I_3\omega_3\hat e_3$ (using the total ω, not a relative spin).
prereqs: ω must be resolved along tilted axes.
Usually how the axes are found.

skills.title: Motion right after an impulsive blow
skills.task: Get $\vec L$ from the angular impulse, then solve $\mathbf I\vec\omega=\vec L$ for $\vec\omega$ using principal axes.
prereqs: L to ω through the principal moments.

skills.title: Steady precession: τ = dL/dt
skills.task: For L of fixed size and tilt turning at rate Ω, use $d\vec L/dt=\vec\Omega\times\vec L$ (only the part perpendicular to Ω changes) and equate it to the torque about a point where unknown forces drop out.
prereqs: L must be written correctly first.
Torque about a fixed point or the CM.
Torques of gravity and contact forces.

skills.title: Euler's equations
skills.task: Write $I_1\dot\omega_1+(I_3-I_2)\omega_2\omega_3=\tau_1$ (and cyclic) in the principal body frame and use them for a body with a torque-free or simple torque.
prereqs: They are τ = dL/dt in the principal basis.

skills.title: Stability about principal axes (tennis racket)
skills.task: Show rotation about the largest or smallest principal axis is stable and about the intermediate one unstable.

skills.title: Free symmetric top, body frame: Ω_b = (I₃−I)ω₃/I
skills.task: For a torque-free symmetric top, show ω₃ is constant and ω precesses around the symmetry axis at $(I_3-I)\omega_3/I$ as seen in the body.

skills.title: Free symmetric top, fixed frame: Ω_s = L/I
skills.task: Seen from the fixed frame, L is constant and the symmetry axis and ω precess around it at $L/I$; ω, L and ê₃ lie in one plane.

skills.title: Euler angles φ, θ, ψ
skills.task: Describe a top's orientation by precession φ, tilt θ and spin ψ, and picture each rotation.

skills.title: ω in Euler angles; ω₃ = ψ̇ + φ̇ cos θ
skills.task: Write $\vec\omega=\dot\phi\hat z+\dot\theta\hat n+\dot\psi\hat e_3$ and its components along the principal axes, e.g. $\omega_3=\dot\psi+\dot\phi\cos\theta$ with θ from the vertical.
prereqs: ẑ resolved along ê₃ and the perpendicular.

skills.title: Heavy top in steady precession
skills.task: Derive $Mg\ell=\Omega(I_3\omega_3-I\Omega\cos\theta)$ with the torque method, I about a perpendicular axis through the pivot.
prereqs: Needs ω₃ and the perpendicular part.

skills.title: Fast top: Ω ≈ Mgℓ/(I₃ω₃)
skills.task: Pick the slow precession root and approximate it for a fast top; explain why faster spin means slower precession.

skills.title: Heavy top by the Lagrangian method
skills.task: Write the top's Lagrangian in Euler angles and use the two conserved momenta (from φ and ψ being cyclic) plus energy.
prereqs: T uses ω in Euler angles.

skills.title: Nutation
skills.task: Describe the tip's bobbing about steady precession and estimate its frequency ($\approx I_3\omega_3/I$ for a fast top).
prereqs: Morin derives it from the Lagrangian.

skills.title: Stability of a vertical (sleeping) top
skills.task: Show a vertical top is stable if $I_3^2\omega_3^2>4IMg\ell$.
prereqs: Uses the same equation near θ = 0.

skills.title: Deriving dimensional scales
skills.task: Match mass, length and time powers to derive time, speed and energy scales for a pendulum, spring or orbit, and predict changes when parameters change.
prereqs: Deriving a scale requires the dimensions of its ingredients.

skills.title: What dimensions can and cannot determine
skills.task: Separate dimensional constraints from unknown constants and functions of dimensionless parameters; identify when amplitude or another ingredient can matter.
prereqs: A dimensionless ratio is identified by cancelling units.

skills.title: Inertia and inertial frames
skills.task: Predict force-free motion, distinguish velocity from acceleration at an instant, and recognize an inertial frame using free-particle motion.

skills.title: Momentum rate, mass and vector acceleration
skills.task: Use net force as momentum rate, state the constant-mass condition for F=ma, compare mass through acceleration, and apply the vector law in its Newtonian domain.
prereqs: Force and acceleration must be compared component by component.

skills.title: Interaction pairs and isolated systems
skills.task: Identify third-law partners on different bodies, relate their accelerations and total momentum, and state the particle-force scope of the third law.
prereqs: Separating bodies helps distinguish a reaction force from the net force.
